name: 993/993 Turbo connecting rod, Ti64 F0 topology concept
description: Independent two-open-flange concept to screen an LPBF Ti-6Al-4V connecting rod. The key dimensions come from a PAUTER/TZR record; outer diameters, flanges, cap split and bolt passages remain F0 assumptions with no commercial surface reused.

classification.intended_use: CAD, DfAM, mass, synthetic loads, nominal stresses and buckling screening only; no manufacturing, installation or engine start-up authorized

provenance.record_license: All rights reserved (see LICENSE) for the concept, the script and the calculations; no photograph, PAUTER/Porsche surface or commercial geometry redistributed

sources.title: TZR Motorsport - manufacturer dimensions of the PAUTER 993/993 Turbo connecting rod
sources.notes: Publishes 127.00 mm center distance, 23.01 mm pin, 58.01 +/- 0.003 mm bore, 18.75/19.58 mm widths, 535 g steel mass, 4340 steel, ARP 2000 bolts and a titanium option advertised at -33%. No surface and no titanium grade. See SRC-TZR-PAUTER-993-CONNECTING-ROD-DIMENSIONS.

sources.title: PorscheFanatics - titanium connecting rods for the 993 engine
sources.notes: Precedent for material choice and candidate only; no geometry and no manufacturing specification. See SRC-PORSCHEFANATICS-993-TITANIUM-CONNECTING-RODS.

sources.title: EOS Titanium Ti64 Grade 5 material data sheet
sources.notes: Provides typical LPBF comparison values that depend on machine, orientation and treatment. They are not connecting-rod fatigue allowables. See SRC-EOS-TI64-GRADE5.

sources.title: TIMETAL 6-4 physical properties
sources.notes: Wrought density, modulus, expansion and specific heat are used for physical screening only; they do not constitute an LPBF material card. See SRC-TIMET-TI64-PHYSICAL-PROPERTIES.

sources.title: elferclassic - 993 Turbo technical data
sources.notes: Documents 100 mm bore, 76.4 mm stroke and 6,720 rpm limiter; cylinder pressure, reciprocating masses and the 100 h cycle remain synthetic. See SRC-ELFERCLASSIC-993-TURBO-TECHNICAL-DATA.

material.grade: Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5 LPBF for screening; PAUTER titanium alloy unknown
material.standard: ASTM F2924 and program-specific connecting rod specification to be contracted

post_processing: powder removal through a fully open topology
stress relief and heat treatment qualified for machine, parameters and orientation
HIP to be decided on defect population and representative fatigue tests
separation and machining of the cap, joint face, bolt bores and seats
machining and finishing of both bores with defined small-end bushing and bearing shells
radiusing, polishing of load paths, end-to-end and set balancing
supplier_requirements: traceable powder, machine, parameters, orientation, lot and powder recycling
oriented coupons with tensile, toughness, fatigue and representative defects after all post-processing
full dimensional analysis of the joint face, center distance, bores, squareness and parallelism
CT of the body and cap, dye penetrant inspection after machining and roughness check
capability evidence on preload, friction, tightening and service life of the selected bolts
proof tests then full-scale fatigue with an approved engine envelope before any dyno run

titanium.alloy: Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5 candidate only; the alloy of the PAUTER option is not published
titanium.heat_treatment: EOS stress relief and ductility treatment to be qualified; no recipe is frozen without supplier, orientation and coupons
machined_surfaces: big-end bore and bearing shell seats
inspection: CT of the body, cap, fillets and flange transitions
full metrology of bores, center distance, joint face, parallelism and squareness
dye penetrant inspection after machining and finishing
roughness, porosity, alpha case, residual stresses and balancing
proof tests and full-scale fatigue with representative bolts, bearing shells and pins
titanium.galvanic_isolation: Qualify titanium-steel couples with bolts, bearing shells and pin, fretting, galling, coatings, lubrication, expansion and galvanic contamination in engine oil.

known_limits: Only the center distance, the two functional diameters, the two widths, the steel mass and the advertised titanium gain come from the PAUTER/TZR record.
The 78/40 mm outer diameters, the two 10 x 14 mm flanges, the cap and the bolt passages are F0 assumptions.
The CAD mass of 341.02 g depends on a synthetic shape and a nominal density; it validates neither the PAUTER gain nor the balancing.
The load case uses a cylinder pressure of 12 MPa, 600 g piston/pin, one third of the rod mass and 100 h, all entirely synthetic.
LPBF is the preferred process only to study the F0 topology; the production choice remains conditional on comparison with forged/machined steel and conventional titanium.
Section stresses, the Kt=1.5 factor and Euler replace neither 3D contact, nor bolt preload, nor bearing shells, nor multiaxial fatigue.
The EOS/TIMET values are ambient and physical comparisons, not hot or fatigue LPBF allowables.
The full-scale Cecchel study reports fatigue below the conventional reference and requires dedicated qualification.
The STEP proves only two re-readable BREP solids; it is authorized neither for manufacturing, nor for installation, nor for an engine.
